directive: **UI** — runs AFTER Features: capture the screens that deliver the defined capabilities as a PLAN, not as code. **Do NOT design or generate the screens yourself** — no skeleton code, no live preview; the visual design comes from the user via Claude Design. Author a **Claude Design kickoff** at `prompts/ui-kickoff.md` — a self-contained brief (product goal, feature→screen map, each screen's purpose/states/flows, design-system constraints) concrete enough that Claude Design can produce the screens without re-asking — and write `ui.md` with the screen inventory. **If the project has a Data Model** (`bsc data model get` — non-null once a migration/data project inferred one), AUTHOR THE KICKOFF FROM IT: map each entity → its screens (list / detail / form), the relationships → navigation between them, and DERIVE EACH ENTITY'S DATA SHAPE MECHANICALLY rather than by eye — `bsc data shapes` reads the same model and returns, per entity, RANKED shape candidates (`list` · `linked-list` · `tree` · `graph` · `table` · `key-value`) each with a confidence and the structural reason it fired (a self-referencing ref → tree, a next/prev link or sequence column → linked-list, a join table → graph, a name+value pair → key-value, otherwise table/list by column density). Lead with the top candidate, but where two candidates tie (a lone self-reference is a tree ONLY if an item has one parent) ASK the user — the schema cannot settle it. Name each screen's chosen shape in the kickoff so the Test UI stage can pick the matching layout, and fold the **Platform Behavior Summary** (`bsc data scan get` — validation rules, Flows/Process Builder, approval processes captured in the Source scan) into the screens' states/flows + validation — so Claude Design produces data-driven screens over the real schema, not generic ones. If the user has DROPPED design files (check `design/intake.json` — the file-intake manifest), they're real Claude Design exports: route each into the UI repo (e.g. `<repo>/src/components/`) and reference them in `prompts/ui-kickoff.md` AND in the UI stream's worker kickoff — so the fleet builds the actual approved design. Then tell the user to take the kickoff to Claude Design and drop the exported `.dc.html` files back into the UI panel, which routes the design and clears the stage.
name: UI

require.label: route the design to the project

blurb: Screens and flows from the features — the user designs them in Claude Design and provides the files.
prompt:
With the features defined, generate a **Claude Design kickoff** the user can paste straight into
a Claude Design session — built FROM the existing planned features. Read the features and write, at
`prompts/ui-kickoff.md`, a self-contained brief: the product goal; the **feature → screen map**
(which screens each feature needs); for each screen its purpose, key states, and primary flows; and
the design-system constraints (tokens, components, layout). Make it concrete enough that Claude
Design can produce the screens without re-asking. Also write `ui.md` with the screen inventory the
Render preview can visualize.

When the project has a Data Model, do not guess how each entity should be rendered: run
`bsc data shapes` (add an entity key for just one, `--pretty` for indented JSON). It infers each
entity's ideal DATA SHAPE from the model's own structure — self-referencing refs, chain links,
join tables, attribute bags, column density — and returns RANKED candidates with a confidence and
a reason, never a single guessed answer. Record the chosen shape per screen; where the top two
candidates are equally plausible, put the question to the user rather than picking silently.

**Do NOT design the screens yourself** — the visual design comes from the user via Claude Design.
Once the kickoff is written, tell the user to take it to Claude Design, design the screens there,
and bring the exported `.dc.html` design files back by dropping them into the UI panel — that routes
the design to the project and clears this stage.

Gate: the Claude Design files are provided and the design is routed to the project.
routePrompt: The user just added files under design/ — see design/intake.json for the manifest. For each staged file: examine it, classify it, and route it to the right place in this project. Use `bsc plan repo list` to pick the relevant repo (e.g. copy design assets into the repo that owns the UI), copy the file into that repo's directory, and reference it in the appropriate section file. In a multi-repo project, only attach UI assets to the UI-bearing repo. If a file's destination is ambiguous, ask me before placing it.
